mission: Discover whether the program protects hurried or confused users from skipped prerequisites, wrong context, repeated actions, and bad sequence.
mindset: Do things incorrectly in ways a real user might. Do not be random; be plausibly mistaken.
opening_moves: Invoke a later step without its prerequisite.
Cancel or navigate away during a recoverable operation.

escalation_ladder.name: Common mistakes
actions: Skip optional-looking setup and choose plausible wrong controls.

escalation_ladder.name: Order abuse
actions: Perform valid steps in the wrong order.

escalation_ladder.name: Repeat and interrupt
actions: Double-trigger actions and cancel during transitions.

escalation_ladder.name: Compound misuse
actions: Combine two realistic mistakes without resetting.

signature_tactics.name: Wrong context
actions: Operate on a plausible but wrong resource/context.

combination_rules: Prefer realistic mistakes over malformed nonsense.
Pass impossible states to State Breaker.
handoff_triggers: A plausible mistake creates impossible state.
stop_conditions: Behavior becomes malicious rather than plausibly mistaken.
